missing_spec_content.spec_text: investigate the effectiveness of different materials as thermal insulators and the factors that may affect the thermal insulation properties of a material.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson's practical only covers comparing different materials. It also lists thickness as a control variable: "The time and the thickness of material are also control variables" (keyPoints[3].content). It never teaches investigating the factors that affect a material's insulating properties, such as thickness or number of layers, as independent variables. That half of the required practical is missing.

factual_errors.text: Wasted energy: energy transferred to a store we don't want, usually thermal or sound
factual_errors.correction: Sound is not an energy store. Energy is transferred by sound waves and ends up dissipated in the thermal store of the surroundings. The lesson itself says this in keyPoints[0].content: "Some is transferred by sound waves. It all ends up in the thermal store of the surroundings." The bullet should say wasted energy is dissipated, so it is stored in less useful ways, usually in the thermal store of the surroundings.

factual_errors.text: Conduction is how heat passes through a solid, from hot to cold.
factual_errors.correction: Conduction also happens in liquids and gases, though much less well than in most solids. The lesson's own explanation that trapped air in loft insulation "reduces conduction and convection" (keyPoints[3].content) depends on conduction happening in a gas. A better wording is that conduction is energy transfer through a material from hotter to colder regions, and it happens best in solids.
